answers.summary: Arnold said obeying God’s commandments leads to righteous acts. He urged doing right and loving God without pretending to be perfect.

questions.question: Did Arnold connect Zechariah’s two anointed ones with Revelation’s witnesses?

answers.summary: Arnold explains the expression as sons of oil and says he believes they are the two witnesses. His explicitly stated belief is retained as such.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider a beard disqualifying for a minister?

answers.summary: Arnold says there is nothing biblically wrong with a minister having a beard and distinguishes his personal preference. He briefly mentions a Nazirite vow without developing the comparison.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider an address containing 666 the mark of the beast?

answers.summary: Arnold says no: allegiance and understanding matter rather than digits on property or skin. He relates the number to his sixth-seal, trumpet and vial interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider an unworshipped Christmas tree an idol?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished a household tree from an idol carved and worshipped in his reading of Jeremiah 10. He appealed to evergreen symbolism and said worship belongs to God, not the tree.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider asking God for help an improper use of God?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that suggestion and encourages honest conversation with God when help is needed. He compares God’s care with a loving parent responding to a child.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider caring for an ill parent service to God?

answers.summary: Arnold strongly reassured a disabled listener caring for his mother that his cooking, cleaning and personal care pleased God. He contrasted that care with giving to a church while neglecting a parent.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider divorce and remarriage an automatic bar to serving as a deacon?

answers.summary: Arnold said a biblically divorced and remarried person has one current spouse, not two. He also emphasized genuine repentance and a changed life rather than permanently excluding someone whom Christ has forgiven.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider preferring privacy or living alone a failure before God?

answers.summary: Arnold said it can be a valid choice and may leave room for focused study and service. He described his own preference for seclusion outside teaching and encouraged the listener to seek God’s direction.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider supporting false doctrine in 2 John 11 unforgivable?

answers.summary: Arnold says the sin described is forgivable and distinguishes it from the unpardonable sin. He nevertheless warns that encouraging or supporting a teacher bringing another doctrine makes someone a participant in that teacher’s work.

questions.question: Did Arnold consider tears of joy a sign of weakness?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and encourages the listener not to accept a guilt trip over tears of joy. He also refers to Jesus weeping in John 11:35 while distinguishing that occasion’s circumstances.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe alcoholism as illness, sin, or both?

answers.summary: Arnold described alcoholism as both disease and harmful overindulgence. He recommended help, including AA, and said calling it a disease did not mean denying moral responsibility. His metabolic explanation is recorded as his statement, not a medical finding.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe Cain as a hybrid?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly answered yes, within his belief that Cain was Satan’s son. This records his interpretation rather than an independently verified ancestry claim.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe God as having a sense of humor?

answers.summary: Arnold said yes and offered his reading of the handwriting on the wall in Daniel as an example. He found the frightened king’s reaction humorous; the detail is his interpretation of the narrative.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe God’s kingdom as already present?

answers.summary: Arnold said Christ is already king and the world his dominion. He also described the kingdom as present in a person through the Holy Spirit, while acknowledging that people can choose deception.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe Mary Magdalene as physically engaged to Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold clarified that he meant spiritual betrothal in the sense in which Christians await Christ’s wedding, not a personal earthly marriage. His historical and language references were not fully documented in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe Revelation 7’s 144,000 as living people at the sealing?

answers.summary: Arnold says they are alive when the four winds are restrained and interprets sealing as teaching God’s word into their minds before the end.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe the giants of his Genesis interpretation as flesh or spiritual beings?

answers.summary: Arnold describes them as flesh hybrids and discusses Goliath and Petra. His height, archaeological and ancestry assertions are not independently established by this FAQ.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe the nations following Satan after the millennium as flesh and blood?

answers.summary: Arnold said they have spiritual bodies because all were changed at the last trumpet. He expected God to destroy those who followed Satan and referred to Matthew 10:28. A Gog-and-Magog comparison in the captions is awkward and is not resolved here.

questions.question: Did Arnold describe the spiritual body as having substance?

answers.summary: Arnold said it has substance rather than being merely air. He used his reading of Genesis 6 as an illustration, without providing physical measurements or a complete account of its nature.

questions.question: Did Arnold equate a modern census with David’s condemned numbering?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and distinguishes public counting from David’s reliance on numbers rather than God. His suggestions about optional answers and licenses are historical comments, not current legal guidance.

questions.question: Did Arnold equate releasing a dove at a funeral with fly-away teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and treats it as a loving church custom using a Holy Spirit symbol. He reassures the bereaved listener about the spirit returning to God.

questions.question: Did Arnold equate saluting the national flag with worshiping another god?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and distinguishes respect for the flag and prior service from worship. He presents saluting as an honor, especially in uniform.

questions.question: Did Arnold expect a loved one’s eye color to remain recognizable in a spiritual body?

answers.summary: Arnold inferred that recognizable family features, including eye color, would remain, appealing to his interpretation of Ezekiel 44. He presented the inference as his opinion and expected everyone to be young adults.

questions.question: Did Arnold expect animals and bodies in eternity to be exactly like those in his first age?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, appealing to Isaiah 11 for animals no longer preying on one another. He described different spiritual bodies and the absence of marriage, without directly confirming that dinosaurs would be present.

questions.question: Did Arnold expect more land in the renewed earth?

answers.summary: Arnold cited Revelation 21:1 and understood the removal of bodies of water as restoring land for those who overcome. This is his reading of the passage.

questions.question: Did Arnold expect new end-time doctrines or covenants?

answers.summary: Arnold says the Holy Spirit’s future testimony will express the existing word rather than replace it with a new doctrine. He relates Ecclesiastes 1, Acts 2, Joel 2 and Mark 13.

questions.question: Did Arnold expect people to remember his proposed first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold expected memory of that age after this life. His speculation about General Patton and possible memories before birth was explicitly described as unwritten and uncertain.

questions.question: Did Arnold give a definite length for the fig-tree generation?

answers.summary: Arnold said many would like to know its exact length but did not provide a number. He urged patience and attention to events.

questions.question: Did Arnold give fixed intervals between Revelation’s trumpets?

answers.summary: Arnold said no fixed interval is stated for every trumpet, but events identify the stages. He described the fifth as teaching, the sixth as the false messiah’s appearance and made an additional interpretive comparison with the thunder in John 12.

questions.question: Did Arnold identify Abel as the first prophet in the Luke 11 discussion?

answers.summary: Arnold agrees with the listener’s identification of Abel as the first prophet and connects his death with Cain. He extends the answer into his disputed ancestry interpretation of later events; those collective ancestry claims are not adopted as historical facts.

questions.question: Did Arnold identify Daniel’s raiser of taxes as a supernatural being?

answers.summary: Arnold identified the figure in Daniel 11:20 as a politician with taxation power rather than a supernatural entity. He placed that figure before the antichrist in his end-time sequence.

questions.question: Did Arnold identify Hagar as a Kenite?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and identifies Hagar as Egyptian, connecting Ishmael with Arab peoples. The later population identification remains his historical interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold identify John the Baptist and the writer called Saint John as the same person?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes John the Baptist from the disciple John. He identifies the Gospel, the epistles and Revelation with that disciple and recalls Jesus entrusting his mother to John.

questions.question: Did Arnold identify Moses’ wife in Numbers 12 as Zipporah?

answers.summary: Arnold identified her as Zipporah and described Jethro as a Midianite descended from Abraham through Keturah. His geographical and ancestry explanation is retained as his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold identify the United States as Babylon in Isaiah 13?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no. He distinguishes the Babylon in Isaiah from his interpretation of Revelation’s mystery Babylon and associates the latter with the false Christ in Jerusalem. Historical event references in the answer are not current announcements.

questions.question: Did Arnold include believers in the great white throne judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold said the great white throne judgment includes both believers and unbelievers, describing it as reward for faithful believers and final judgment after the millennium for those refusing God. He associated fine linen with righteous acts.

questions.question: Did Arnold include deceived human followers in the locust army?

answers.summary: Arnold said others would support the fallen angels because they mistakenly believed the false Christ was Jesus. He encouraged believers to understand the sequence and trust God rather than fear that army.

questions.question: Did Arnold include overcoming believers of all nations among those serving Christ in the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold affirmed that elect believers from the nations stand against Satan and rejected the premise that they must wait until eternity to approach Christ. He included them among the Zadok and described roles serving their own peoples.

questions.question: Did Arnold include sealed believers among those tormented for five months in Revelation 9?

answers.summary: Arnold said Revelation 9:4 excludes those bearing God’s seal from that torment. He connected their authority with allowing the Holy Spirit to speak when delivered up and warned against premeditating the testimony.

questions.question: Did Arnold interpret the wedding of Christ as physical or spiritual?

answers.summary: Arnold answers spiritual. His brief answer also mentions judgment without fully distinguishing the events’ timing.

questions.question: Did Arnold know what happened to Solomon’s gold?

answers.summary: Arnold did not give a definite account of Solomon’s gold, saying temples had used gold and expressing uncertainty. His ensuing anecdote concerned the wilderness rather than a documented answer about Solomon.

questions.question: Did Arnold mention illness among people close to Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold initially said the disciples themselves were not sick but cited Peter’s ill mother-in-law being healed. He did not give an exhaustive medical history of the disciples, and later comments about disagreements concerned a different issue.

questions.question: Did Arnold object to cooking with vinegar because it was offered to Jesus?

answers.summary: Arnold says cooking with vinegar is acceptable. He distinguishes culinary vinegar from his account of the wine offered at the crucifixion.

questions.question: Did Arnold object to gathering at Christmas if he dated Christ’s conception rather than birth then?

answers.summary: Arnold treated the conception as Christ beginning to dwell with people and referred to John’s response in Elizabeth’s womb. He directed listeners to his Christmas study for his calendar calculation rather than objecting to the family gathering.

questions.question: Did Arnold object to musical instruments in worship?

answers.summary: Arnold approved instruments, citing David’s harp. He said the message conveyed matters more than whether music is accompanied, and objected to degrading content regardless of instrument or voice.

questions.question: Did Arnold object to praying that a deceased parent has peace?

answers.summary: Arnold said the prayer would do no harm and encouraged talking to God about the parent. He also explained that prayer can be silent and offered anywhere.

questions.question: Did Arnold prohibit reading the Bible from beginning to end?

answers.summary: Arnold did not prohibit it. He advised studying in whatever order the listener felt led, emphasizing careful understanding rather than reading merely to finish.

questions.question: Did Arnold prohibit touching leather made from swine?

answers.summary: Arnold said he distinguished using leather from eating swine and did not prohibit the former. He appealed to his reading of Leviticus 11; this is his interpretation rather than an exhaustive account of all contact rules.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend affiliated Shepherd’s Chapel churches?

answers.summary: Arnold says this ministry is independent and that other churches using its teaching are not branches for which it is accountable. He encourages checking claims about what he teaches against his recorded teaching and discusses why the ministry copyrights its work.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend asking a non-Christian to perform baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold discouraged involving a non-Christian, partly because of the risk of making the act a mockery. He affirmed that one Christian may baptize another, though some denominations may not recognize it.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend cursing someone who repeatedly takes another person’s belongings?

answers.summary: Arnold says a curse is unnecessary and advises putting a stop to the taking. The closing words of the answer are incomplete in the captions, so no specific remedy is inferred.

questions.question: Did Arnold recommend relying on relatives to help after death rather than believing now?

answers.summary: Arnold strongly discourages postponing faith in expectation of later family help. He urges the listener to accept God and help others rather than depend on them to secure salvation.

questions.question: Did Arnold regard military service as incompatible with loving enemies?

answers.summary: Arnold said no and defended honorable service as protecting freedom, families and worship. He compared correction with love, while not analyzing every possible military action or order in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold relate the breath of life in Adam to the Comforter?

answers.summary: Arnold answered that in a sense he did, because God’s breath is the breath of life. The answer was brief and did not develop a complete distinction between these terms.

questions.question: Did Arnold require asking an offended person for forgiveness in every case?

answers.summary: Arnold said to ask God and use judgment about approaching the other person, considering danger or additional harm. He expected a sincere Christian to be willing to forgive but warned that not everyone claiming that label would respond well.

questions.question: Did Arnold require men and women to sit separately in church?

answers.summary: Arnold said the Bible does not require front or back seating by sex. He called it a church tradition and encouraged the listener to think independently if uncomfortable with it.

questions.question: Did Arnold require naming every sin individually when repenting?

answers.summary: Arnold said sincere repentance for all sins does not require remembering and listing every one. He emphasized meaning the change of heart rather than a formula or an exhaustive memory.

questions.question: Did Arnold require physical circumcision for salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold said no. He interpreted present circumcision as of the heart or mind, applying to women and men who believe in Christ, and reassured the elderly man in the question.

questions.question: Did Arnold require public annual repentance?

answers.summary: Arnold says to repent to Christ promptly after sin rather than wait for an annual public event. He rejects exposing forgiven matters for public gossip.

questions.question: Did Arnold require rebaptism after being baptized by a false teacher?

answers.summary: Arnold treated sincere baptism as a matter between the believer and Christ rather than the minister. He said rebaptism was unnecessary if the believer understood its purpose, while allowing it if the person remained troubled.

questions.question: Did Arnold require shouting for God to hear prayer?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, explaining that God knows thoughts and can hear silent prayer. He emphasized order and discipline rather than volume or screaming.

questions.question: Did Arnold require someone to walk to an altar alone for salvation or baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that requirement as a human tradition. He reassured the listener that having her aunt or mother accompany her did not invalidate sincere faith or baptism.

questions.question: Did Arnold reserve forgiveness of sins to the apostles?

answers.summary: Arnold said Christ is the one who forgives sins. He encouraged asking the Father for forgiveness in Jesus’ name and connected direct access to God with the torn temple veil.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a deceased person can remain on earth as a ghost?

answers.summary: Arnold said the person returns to God rather than remaining as a ghost. He distinguished this from evil spiritual influence that he believed could operate if God allowed it.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a listener must admit religious visitors to her home?

answers.summary: Arnold says the listener may decline or ask visitors to leave. He distinguishes God’s judgment from a visitor’s authority and says teachers should document their claims from Scripture.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a person must remain with abusive relatives in heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured the listener that heaven would not force continued abuse and spoke categorically against abusers being there. That categorical statement is preserved as his answer and flagged for comparison with passages where he leaves individual judgment to God.

questions.question: Did Arnold say a salt covenant requires staying in a church whose teaching one rejects?

answers.summary: Arnold suggests the covenant was properly to God rather than an organization and says the listener is free to leave if the ministry does not represent God. He objects to using a covenant as pressure to remain.

questions.question: Did Arnold say age or disability reduces a person’s worth to God?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no, criticizes impatience toward older people and encourages respect and assistance. He reassures the listener that God loves his children regardless of age.

questions.question: Did Arnold say babies inherit sin through DNA?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the claim and describes children as innocent before an age of accountability. He refers to Jesus welcoming children. His answer expresses his teaching on responsibility rather than a genetic explanation of behavior.

questions.question: Did Arnold say believers must stop communion or take it secretly during the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Arnold said believers may continue communion and need not hide it. He urged remaining ready for testimony and not letting another person stop the practice.

questions.question: Did Arnold say birth outside marriage excludes a child from heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold said the parents’ sin does not fall on the child and that birth outside marriage does not exclude salvation or heavenly service. He distinguished this from his interpretation of the Hebrew word mamzar.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Christ returns without touching earth?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that claim. He expected Christ to return to earth, touch down and establish his kingdom, rather than remain away while removing a few believers.

questions.question: Did Arnold say fallen angels can appear as children?

answers.summary: Arnold says no, distinguishing being cast out in an existing body from birth through a woman. His separate comments about spirits entering children are religious claims, not a diagnosis of any child.

questions.question: Did Arnold say fallen angels must be born of women?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, describing their offense as leaving their habitation to seduce women rather than entering flesh through birth. He referred to Jude and connected their offspring with his interpretation of Noah’s flood.

questions.question: Did Arnold say family disapproval determines whether someone reaches heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold says only God judges that outcome. He acknowledges part of the listener’s story is missing and does not infer what the reported call and return meant.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God can forgive angry words spoken after a child dies?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured a bereaved parent that God loves and forgives his children. He encouraged renewed love for God and said the deceased child was with him, rather than declaring the parent beyond forgiveness.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God intervenes for people with free will when asked?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes when they ask, while distinguishing his belief that God intervenes in the elect’s lives without their asking. He links that distinction with Romans 8 and responsibility at judgment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say God still heals people today?

answers.summary: Arnold says God remains a healer and encourages the listener to pray. He also mentions anointing. The answer expresses his belief and prayer for the listener; it does not establish that a healing occurred.

questions.question: Did Arnold say growing up without an earthly father prevents loving God?

answers.summary: Arnold said it does not, referring to his own upbringing away from his father. He urged personal responsibility and providing a good example to one’s own children.

questions.question: Did Arnold say humans could kill Satan when he appears?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and places Satan’s final destruction under God’s authority. He distinguishes the death of the flesh from the second death and refers to Matthew 10:28 and Ezekiel 28.

questions.question: Did Arnold say hybrid DNA from his fallen-angel interpretation survives today?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and says the flood destroyed those hybrids while preserving the ark’s occupants. These are his ancestry claims, not established genetics.

questions.question: Did Arnold say imperfect Bible pronunciation endangers salvation?

answers.summary: Arnold reassures the listener that understanding the message and loving God matter, and acknowledges his own pronunciation difficulties.

questions.question: Did Arnold say loved ones can help someone who died without overcoming?

answers.summary: Arnold places such help in the millennium rather than the present. He warns against assuming knowledge of a dying person’s final thoughts and describes the elect helping relatives under his interpretation of Ezekiel 44. The captioned verse span needs confirmation.

questions.question: Did Arnold say memories of past sins mean a person is not saved?

answers.summary: Arnold said remembering a forgiven mistake is natural experience that can prevent repetition. He distinguished memory from continuing guilt and urged the listener not to doubt Christ’s saving work.

questions.question: Did Arnold say nail prints would distinguish the true Christ from the antichrist?

answers.summary: Arnold says the antichrist was not crucified but warns against relying on what a deceiver might display. He instead emphasizes his teaching that the false Christ comes at the sixth trumpet and the true Christ at the seventh.

questions.question: Did Arnold say people in heaven can visit earth whenever they want?

answers.summary: Arnold does not describe unrestricted visits. He says such a visit would occur if God chose someone to deliver a message.

questions.question: Did Arnold say people need to forgive themselves?

answers.summary: Arnold said yes and warned against treating oneself as too good to have sinned. He connected self-forgiveness with repentance and explicitly said God would not forgive someone who would not forgive themselves. That qualification is preserved separately from other reassurance passages for comparison.

questions.question: Did Arnold say people on different sides of paradise’s gulf can see one another?

answers.summary: Arnold says the rich man seeing Lazarus supports visibility across the gulf. He then describes the elect helping relatives during the millennium under his interpretation of Ezekiel 44. He does not clearly establish unrestricted present communication.

questions.question: Did Arnold say people will know they have changed into spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold said they will know because the seventh trumpet will have sounded and Christ will be present. He also affirmed that remaining in flesh indicates the true Christ has not returned.

questions.question: Did Arnold say religious people can also be spiritually blinded?

answers.summary: Arnold said outward religious habits do not guarantee love for God or willingness to hear Scripture. He criticized divisive traditions and advised testing a teacher’s fruit rather than trusting religious appearances.

questions.question: Did Arnold say salvation requires speaking in tongues?

answers.summary: Arnold ultimately says someone can reach heaven without speaking in the cloven tongue, while distinguishing those he calls the elect or firstfruits. He describes Pentecost’s speech as understandable in every language and contrasts it with speech requiring interpretation. The opening caption wording is inconsistent, so that qualification is retained.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan can actually change people into spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold said Satan cannot give life or effect the genuine change into spiritual bodies. He distinguished that inability from Satan’s capacity to make things appear otherwise.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan could fool believers into thinking they had changed into spiritual bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and contrasts vulnerable flesh with what he describes as a perfected spiritual body free from ordinary gravity. These physical descriptions are his beliefs, not independently established properties.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan is present before being openly seen in the five-month period?

answers.summary: Arnold affirmed presence during the first two and a half months but said he might not be seen then. He said the two witnesses would keep believers informed. The listener’s Mount of Olives premise is not separately documented in the answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan retains spiritual influence while bound during the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold says the restraint is complete, including spiritual influence, until the short season. He explicitly calls Michael’s role in the imprisonment his opinion and describes that period as easier for teaching.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan returns after the millennium in the antichrist office?

answers.summary: Arnold says no, interpreting Revelation 19:20 as destruction of the beast and false-prophet offices before the millennium. He distinguishes Satan’s later release from having those same offices or authority.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan would be released in 2012?

answers.summary: Arnold explicitly denied having predicted Satan’s release in 2012. He distinguished his teaching about the fig-tree generation from naming a particular year and described the Mayan calendar concern as the end of a calendar segment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan would torture believers into receiving the mark?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured a fearful new believer that Satan would present himself as a saving Christ and deceive through apparent love rather than appear as a torturer. He emphasized God’s protection in his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Satan’s appearance aged or changed from creation?

answers.summary: Arnold said angels do not age and described Satan as retaining the beauty he read in Ezekiel 28. He attributed Satan’s fall to pride and the heart rather than physical aging.

questions.question: Did Arnold say serious past wrongdoing prevents someone from being elect?

answers.summary: Arnold used Paul’s persecution and conversion to illustrate that God can use someone who has turned from wrongdoing. He affirmed the possibility while warning against treating a sinful past as a credential.

questions.question: Did Arnold say Shem, Ham and Japheth were triplets?

answers.summary: Arnold said they were separate single births, not triplets. He did not supply their individual birth dates in this answer.

questions.question: Did Arnold say someone with past sins can still be saved?

answers.summary: Arnold answers yes and says everyone falls short. He describes sincere repentance as a change of heart and mind, gratitude for forgiveness and receiving a clean slate.

questions.question: Did Arnold say testimony before the antichrist happens in groups?

answers.summary: Arnold says groups, interpreting the ten-day trial language as an individual maximum within a longer period. The exact Revelation reference he recalls needs checking.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the absence of a visible visitor at death means a person was abandoned?

answers.summary: Arnold reassured a bereaved mother that she would not necessarily see activity in a different spiritual dimension. He did not treat the absence of a visible sign as evidence that her son lacked help.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the antichrist can force a sealed believer to believe in him?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, while warning that Satan can make things appear otherwise than they are. He emphasized knowing the order of events, trusting the Holy Spirit and the protection he read in Revelation 9:4. Part of the listener’s wording is unclear.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the antichrist must arrive in May?

answers.summary: Arnold affirms a five-month period but says the stage of the locust must be recognized before counting. He refers listeners to upcoming historical Passover messages rather than giving an unqualified May-arrival rule.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the antichrist was already personally on earth in this broadcast?

answers.summary: Arnold said no, while distinguishing present evil spiritual influence from Satan’s future personal arrival. He expected that arrival to be publicly celebrated as a religious deliverer rather than concealed.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the beings called Geber in the captions had souls?

answers.summary: Arnold answers that every entity has a soul and discusses an opportunity to respond properly. The caption term Geber needs confirmation against the audio before a more specific identification is assigned.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the flowers in his studio were real, and did he require them in worship?

answers.summary: Arnold confirmed that the studio flowers were fresh and expressed gratitude for their beauty and God’s creation. He did not establish the listener’s proposed requirement that worship must include fresh flowers.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the great falling away had already begun?

answers.summary: Arnold says deception is already present in part through teachings he considers human traditions. He distinguishes that preparation from the great falling away when Satan appears in person.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the sixth seal had begun in this recording?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and says he considers it close, with events still to occur. That statement belongs to this historical recording and is not a current assessment.

questions.question: Did Arnold say the spiritual body is already present during flesh life?

answers.summary: Arnold answers yes and describes the spiritual body as dwelling within the flesh body and departing when the silver cord breaks. He distinguishes the soul, or self, from its spirit, which he calls the intellect.

questions.question: Did Arnold say those struck by the final hailstones miss judgment?

answers.summary: Arnold says everyone comes to judgment. He places the hailstones at the end of this earth age and says the change to spiritual bodies means those bodies are not harmed by them.

questions.question: Did Arnold say which insects and worms would be present in heaven?

answers.summary: Arnold did not give a definite list. He emphasized the changed conditions of Isaiah 11, including animals no longer being carnivorous, and acknowledged limits to what he could infer.

questions.question: Did Arnold support an unmarried mother dedicating her child to God?

answers.summary: Arnold answers positively and says a parent’s sin is not placed on the child, referring to Jeremiah 31:29. The other recalled legal reference is uncertain and not supplied as precise documentation.

questions.question: Did Arnold support children being baptized in another Christian church?

answers.summary: Arnold says yes when the children understand baptism as publicly affirming Christ’s death and resurrection. He says one Christian can baptize another and encourages the parent’s support.

questions.question: Did Arnold support donating a body to medical science?

answers.summary: Arnold calls the proposed donation honorable and says the person will not need the flesh body after death. He describes the spiritual body as free from the listener’s disease. This reports his pastoral answer rather than medical or legal donation instructions.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that a child lost before birth is born into this earth age again?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no. He says the spirit is already present and that a person passes through this earth age only once.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that all people descend from Adam and Eve?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and appeals to separate creation days and the genealogies of Genesis 4–5. His claimed scientific support is not independently established here; the entry records his interpretation.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that angels can read a person’s mind?

answers.summary: Arnold said neither angels nor Satan can read minds; he reserved that knowledge to God. He then emphasized that God’s complete knowledge makes his judgment fair, including reward for faithful service.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that apostles or ministers must remain unmarried?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no, points to Peter’s mother-in-law in Mark 1:30 and says some teachers were married while others were not. He also discusses Aquila and Priscilla as married teachers.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that everyone will be the same age in eternity?

answers.summary: Arnold said all would be the same age in the third earth age, as he also believed they were in the first age.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that God sends curses or burdens on people?

answers.summary: Arnold uses Jeremiah 23:33 to distinguish God lifting burdens from people bringing trouble on themselves. He says God may withdraw intervention and rejects the idea that another person can place a spiritual curse on a Christian.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that Lilith was Adam’s first wife?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects the idea as mythology and explicitly offers his opinion about why the story arose. That proposed scholarly motive is not established history.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that Noah’s flood covered the whole earth?

answers.summary: Arnold says it probably did not cover the whole world. He explains its extent through his interpretation of its purpose in Genesis 6.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people communicate in paradise?

answers.summary: Arnold answered yes and said people recognize family members who have died. He described the departed as alive with the Father despite bodily death and referred to communication on both sides of paradise.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people in his first earth age lacked souls?

answers.summary: Arnold rejected that premise, saying every living person has a soul. He explained Satan stealing souls as deception drawing people from God rather than removing the existence of a soul.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that people killed one another in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no because he describes them as spiritual beings whose final destruction only God can cause. He refers to Matthew 10:28.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that spiritual bodies reproduced in the first earth age?

answers.summary: Arnold answers that there were no reproductive organs in that age and distinguishes it from this age and his account of fallen angels. This is his theological explanation rather than a verified biological description.

questions.question: Did Arnold teach that the antichrist is a human later inhabited by Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that account and identifies the antichrist with Satan himself, whom he describes as a supernatural cherub. He connects it with Ezekiel 28 and warns that expecting only an ordinary man could contribute to deception.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell a child Christ would return when the child turned thirteen?

answers.summary: Arnold gave no such date and said only the Lord knows the time. He did not know the child’s current age from the letter.

questions.question: Did Arnold tell new believers to leave an unbelieving spouse?

answers.summary: Arnold said not automatically. Citing 1 Corinthians 7:13, he supported remaining together when the spouse does not prevent the believer or children from studying and practicing faith, and emphasized a good example.

questions.question: Did Arnold think a person in heaven would have regrets?

answers.summary: Arnold gives his opinion that someone who makes it to heaven would be happy rather than regretful. He labels this as his own opinion.

questions.question: Did Arnold think Cain knew who his father was in Arnold’s serpent-seed interpretation?

answers.summary: Arnold said probably not, emphasizing innocence. He repeated his interpretation of Genesis 3–4 but did not claim direct evidence of Cain’s personal knowledge.

questions.question: Did Arnold think someone with spiritual understanding could fail to notice an evil influence?

answers.summary: Arnold calls it possible and says people may not recognize what contributes to a fall. This records his spiritual explanation without diagnosing an individual as having an evil spirit.

questions.question: Did Arnold think the antichrist could be a woman?

answers.summary: Arnold said no because he identified the antichrist as Satan himself, whom he described as male. He also rejected identifying that figure as an ordinary person born of a woman.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat eating a rare steak as eating forbidden blood?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished proper bleeding at slaughter from how thoroughly a clean animal’s steak is cooked. He said a rare steak was not the prohibition’s target; this records his religious interpretation rather than food-safety guidance.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat Matthew 24 and Mark 13 as fully fulfilled in AD 70?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that interpretation and centers the chapters on Christ’s return and the fig-tree generation. His answer does not separately analyze every historical layer of the passages.

questions.question: Did Arnold treat seventy times seven as a lifetime forgiveness limit?

answers.summary: Arnold says no and interprets it as sincere repentance being forgiven each time, while warning against a merely pretended change of heart.

questions.question: Did Dennis require flowing water for baptism?

answers.summary: Dennis said a baptismal tank is acceptable. He distinguished the water from cleansing through Christ’s blood, while explaining his preference for the Chapel’s outdoor baptisms at Spavinaw Creek.

questions.question: Does backsliding require being baptized again?

answers.summary: Arnold answers no and tells the listener to repent. He says Christ’s salvation did not fail when the believer drifted away.

questions.question: Does the antichrist come from Africa?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects that interpretation. He says Revelation’s lion imagery concerns deception and identifies Revelation 12 as his explanation of Satan being cast from heaven.

questions.question: How certain was Arnold about the kind of gopher wood used for the ark?

answers.summary: Arnold says the exact wood is unknown and proposes a resinous wood such as pine or cypress. His uncertainty is retained rather than assigning a definite species.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a family struggling with an adult son’s alcohol addiction?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer and uses the prodigal son as an example of someone recognizing the need to change after hardship. He continues his earlier advice against enabling the behavior. This records his pastoral response, not a clinical treatment plan.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a listener not learning Scripture at her church?

answers.summary: Arnold declined to decide whether she should leave, saying God might have a purpose for her there. He recommended prayer and close reading of 2 John to inform her conscience and decision.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a new believer whose bereaved father would not attend church?

answers.summary: Arnold warned that pushing can drive someone away and advised gentle encouragement. He recommended learning his teaching about the dead to offer comfort concerning the father’s deceased mother.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a parent who did not want an adult child’s drug-using partner in her home?

answers.summary: Arnold supports the parent’s right to set a boundary in her own home and not admit the partner. He treats that as protecting the household rather than rejecting her daughter.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise a student concerned about a friend smoking marijuana?

answers.summary: Arnold urges caution about the friendship and objects to the conduct as unlawful and potentially leading to other drug use. Those are his historical pastoral and legal claims, not a statement of current law or an individual medical assessment.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise Bible study for someone at a crossroads?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends choosing a biblical book and reading it chapter by chapter rather than studying in confusion. He mentions prophets but does not prescribe an individual life decision.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise correcting a disrespectful child?

answers.summary: Arnold stresses love, explanation and never correcting in anger. He supports limited physical discipline while also allowing other methods; this paraphrase preserves his stance without turning it into instructions for striking a child.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise discussing rapture teaching in a church that teaches it?

answers.summary: Arnold warned that confrontation as a guest may be unproductive. He allowed gentle discussion in a Bible study and said the listener should consider moving on if convicted to do so, while declining to choose a church for him.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise distinguishing true teaching from false teaching?

answers.summary: Arnold advises comparing teaching with Scripture and reading in context, including time, audience and subject. He urges listeners to study rather than rely solely on a teacher’s claim.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise finding people who follow the true Christ?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer, sound judgment and meeting with believers while acknowledging good people can be found in many places. He emphasizes discernment rather than a guaranteed venue.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise handling a relative’s rude or vulgar talk in the listener’s home?

answers.summary: Arnold supports setting household boundaries instead of passively tolerating the language. He also encourages living an example and allowing for possible change rather than forcing a discussion.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise looking up chief prince in Ezekiel 38?

answers.summary: Arnold corrected the listener’s use of the Greek dictionary and directed her to the Hebrew entry for chief in Ezekiel 38:2. The subsequent name and historical-language wording is damaged in the captions and is not reconstructed here.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise preparing to stand against Satan?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends prayer, studying Scripture and putting on the spiritual armor described in Ephesians 6. He describes the struggle as spiritual rather than against flesh.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise responding to persecution?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages prayer, wise avoidance of persecutors where possible and being wise as a serpent and gentle as a dove. He does not give a definite reason why some face more persecution than others.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone meeting an atheist family member?

answers.summary: Arnold advised demonstrating Christian character and genuine care rather than expecting Scripture alone to persuade someone who rejects it. He offered 1 Corinthians 10:13 for the listener’s own encouragement.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone repeatedly committing the same sin?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages honest prayer for strength to stop, rather than asking forgiveness without addressing the repeated conduct. He warns that an unaddressed weakness can become a means of deception.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone struggling to understand Revelation?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged studying Revelation with guided teaching rather than abandoning it for another book. He noted Daniel’s relationship to Revelation, but said a teacher could help the listener understand the revealing itself.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone wanting God in her life?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages sincere repentance, accepting forgiveness and forgiving oneself. He reassures the listener of God’s love and continuing presence.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone who did not know how to pray?

answers.summary: Arnold describes prayer as honest conversation with the Father, aloud or silently. He emphasizes trust that God hears and recommends asking according to God’s will, while acknowledging that the answer may differ from what the person wants.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone who felt unsure of her faith?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages belief in Jesus as God’s Son, studying Scripture and speaking to God from the heart. He reassures the listener that no one remembers every passage and that Scripture remains available to consult.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise someone who had made a vow to God?

answers.summary: Arnold says a promise to God should be kept. He distinguishes that from imitating Old Testament vows without understanding the duties he believes God gives believers today.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise teaching a child about Passover?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the parent to 1 Corinthians 5:7–8 and emphasizes Christ as Passover rather than an egg hunt.

questions.question: How did Arnold advise women facing degrading name-calling?

answers.summary: Arnold rejects abusive name-calling and encourages strength and self-respect. He cites women such as Deborah and recommends his Women of the Bible study; the answer does not provide a specific safety plan.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a bereaved listener who also asked about his Marine service?

answers.summary: Arnold comforts the listener by saying his mother is with the Father and that they will be reunited. He also expresses gratitude for serving in the Marine Corps and discusses his opposition to communism and socialism.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking whether animals can be angels?

answers.summary: Arnold spoke of animals having spiritual form and being present in God’s future order, referring to Isaiah 11. The captions initially say angels before clarifying animals, so this answer does not establish that animals are heavenly messengers.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking whether God is angry when people do not study?

answers.summary: Arnold said God is pleased when people study and recognized differing appetites for study. He added that neglecting God’s word entirely displeases God.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child asking who God’s father is?

answers.summary: Arnold appealed to God’s declaration I am that I am and said God is what he wishes to be. He did not identify a parent for God, instead saying fuller understanding would come later.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a child worried that moving would mean abandoning a church ministry?

answers.summary: Arnold said he did not know the family’s circumstances or whether another calling was involved. He suggested that pastors remain able to minister after moving rather than assuming their calling ends.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a family considering bankruptcy after an injury?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished unavoidable hardship after injury from using bankruptcy simply to evade debts. He said it may be the remaining option when no other way exists and urged prayerful consideration. This is historical pastoral advice, not a legal or financial assessment of a present case.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a household worried about disability support during the antichrist period?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends keeping a reasonably stocked pantry and reassures the household to care for themselves and trust God. He does not give a prediction about whether their disability payments will continue.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener about protecting family from an intruder?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized protecting one’s family, cited 1 Timothy 5:8, and insisted on obeying civil law and making certain of the person’s identity. This records his historical pastoral answer rather than a determination of lawful force in a present situation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener asking about a fig tree on the studio set?

answers.summary: Arnold responded humorously about spare fig leaves and said the visible plant was not the fig tree the listener assumed. The plant names in this caption export are uncertain and are not confidently identified here.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener describing severe depression and suicidal thoughts?

answers.summary: Arnold responded forcefully with encouragement about God’s love, purpose and power over enemies, and referred to 1 Corinthians 10:13. He did not discuss clinical assessment or crisis care in this answer. This historical pastoral response is not adequate stand-alone guidance for someone at immediate risk; the Luke chapter recalled in the captions is uncertain.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener who skips long lists of names?

answers.summary: Arnold allows for differing interests and duties and says the lists often provide chronology. He does not condemn the listener for finding those passages difficult or boring.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener wishing to go back and change the past?

answers.summary: Arnold frames the concern as difficulty forgiving oneself and uses Paul as an example of remorse. He emphasizes sincere repentance and forgiveness rather than promising time travel or a chance to redo events.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener worried that other nations were taking Israel’s blessings?

answers.summary: Arnold interpreted the concern within his end-time and national-identity teaching but said blessings come from God and cannot be taken away by Satan. The listener’s broad claim about other peoples is not independently established.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a listener’s comparison of deception across three periods?

answers.summary: Arnold agrees with the listener’s comparison of deception in a former age, the antichrist period and the final test after the millennium. He cites Revelation 12 for the one-third imagery. The comparison is his interpretation and is not treated as an independently established account of who experiences each event.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about a Feast of Tabernacles gathering?

answers.summary: Arnold announced television communion and two in-person services, with reservations and no meal provision. These were plans for that historical broadcast period, not a current event schedule.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about being saved through childbirth?

answers.summary: Arnold praises witnessing childbirth as potentially moving a person toward faith. He does not provide a full interpretation of the biblical phrase or claim that giving birth automatically confers salvation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about British royalty and Judah?

answers.summary: Arnold connects British and Russian royal families with Judah in his interpretation of ancestry and migration. The caption passage contains uncertain names and historical assertions; this is an attributed account of his answer, not verified genealogy or history.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about calling no man father in Matthew 23:9?

answers.summary: Arnold declined to criticize the denomination named in the letter. He urged the listener to understand and follow the Scripture, acknowledging imperfections in all denominations, but did not give a detailed interpretation of the title in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Jesus’ age and calendar dates?

answers.summary: Arnold maintained an age of thirty-three and suggested a birth date closer to 2 BC than 4 BC. He did not fully reconcile the listener’s calendar calculation in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about losing constitutional freedom of worship?

answers.summary: Arnold strongly expresses confidence in defending freedom of worship and refers to military service and broadcasting. This is his historical conviction rather than a present legal guarantee or a supplied prophecy of future rights.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about man not living alone?

answers.summary: Arnold first suggests the listener may mean not living by bread alone, citing Luke 4:4 and Deuteronomy 8:3. He also acknowledges Adam receiving Eve as a companion. The answer keeps both possibilities rather than selecting an unstated intended question.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about observing the Feast of Tabernacles today?

answers.summary: Arnold calls the ministry’s observance a fall fellowship and describes it as the start of the civil year on God’s calendar. The brief answer does not provide a full set of observance instructions.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Palestine and Syria’s tribal origins?

answers.summary: Arnold briefly associated them with Ishmael without supplying evidence or addressing the question’s full political premise. This broad ancestry claim is not independently established and should not be used to classify present individuals.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about requests for money for homeless children?

answers.summary: With time running out, Arnold directs the listener to 2 John. He does not develop an answer that would establish a general rule for charitable giving in this passage.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Scripture and memory difficulties?

answers.summary: Arnold encourages studying Scripture, exercising the mind, caring for health and praying. He acknowledges illness and gives no specific verse or established treatment for dementia.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about the prince’s portion in the Companion Bible plan?

answers.summary: Arnold mentions the Savior as prince and also David as prince of Israel. The captioned question about the plan, area and occupants is damaged, so the answer does not establish a clear allocation of that portion.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about the Shroud of Turin?

answers.summary: Arnold considers the proposed identification with Jesus’ burial cloth possible and discusses the image in response to the listener. His assertion about whether it had been disproved is not a verified assessment of the evidence or a current scientific finding.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about the size of paradise’s gulf?

answers.summary: Arnold describes it as a boundary no one may cross by God’s order, not a distance measured in the answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about Truman, MacArthur and the Chosin Reservoir?

answers.summary: Arnold expresses respect for both men while saying MacArthur received poor field intelligence. He credits General Smith and supporting forces with protecting supply lines and helping troops survive. This is his recollection and assessment, not an independently checked military history.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question about wishing on stars and lucky pennies?

answers.summary: Arnold responded lightly to the penny superstition, then redirected the listener toward prayer, loving God and trusting his guidance rather than relying on luck. He did not give a direct blanket prohibition on wishes.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a question comparing biblical and present calendars?

answers.summary: Arnold discusses BC and AD and favors solar reckoning. His brief account does not establish that ancient and current calendars are identical in all details.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request about not wishing bad on false teachers?

answers.summary: Arnold says he cannot recall the requested prohibition and directs the listener to Ezekiel 13’s judgment of false teachers. This records his response without turning it into permission to mistreat anyone.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request for a decree or sign about prayer?

answers.summary: Arnold assumes the listener means a fleece, compares it with Gideon and recommends praying, trying, correcting failures and recognizing when a different course is needed. He advises God’s will rather than a guaranteed prayer formula.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request for studying other religions?

answers.summary: Arnold recommends concentrating on Scripture and suggests a general encyclopedia for comparative information. He does not identify or review a particular other religion in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a request to broadcast the ministry documentaries for home recording?

answers.summary: Arnold says the request will be considered and discusses recording and interpretation work still in progress. He makes no confirmed schedule in this historical answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a seriously ill listener about being unable to tolerate chemotherapy?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized the listener’s personal decision and prayer for God’s will. He spoke of the possibility of divine help while explicitly declining to promise it. This summarizes a historical pastoral response; it is not a treatment recommendation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer a widow angry about circumstances left by her husband?

answers.summary: Arnold acknowledges limited knowledge of the situation, encourages forgiveness and prayer, and urges the listener to seek peace. His assumptions about her husband’s motives are not treated as established facts.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer about a person dying under the influence of drugs?

answers.summary: Arnold declined to determine anyone’s final judgment. He suggested that God takes impaired decision-making into account and judges what a person did with a sound mind, while leaving the individual’s fate in God’s hands.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer about baptism for an adult unable to understand or choose it?

answers.summary: Arnold reassures the mother that her son is in innocence. He emphasizes personal understanding and choice in baptism rather than an outward dipping performed without that understanding.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer about eclipses and possible prophetic signs?

answers.summary: Arnold encouraged watching alignments and seasons without declaring the listener’s proposed 2014–15 eclipses a definite fulfillment. The cited eruption date and calendar correlations were not independently verified in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer about people who died without hearing Scripture?

answers.summary: Arnold appealed to Romans 1:20 and the knowledge of right and wrong available through creation. He emphasized the character shown in their lives, but did not directly locate their holding place in this particular answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer about wishing a boss well despite religious disagreement?

answers.summary: Arnold told the listener to use personal conviction and judgment. He discouraged turning the workplace into religious contention and suggested the listener was capable of handling an ordinary interaction. The captioned question does not fully explain the workplace dispute.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer an abuse survivor challenging born into what we deserve?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes that God loves and can use the listener and that she can move beyond the circumstances. He does not give evidence that she caused or deserved her parents’ abuse; the troubling premise is left unresolved.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer an anointing question when olive oil is unavailable?

answers.summary: Arnold says God understands when oil is unavailable and that the person can explain the situation and ask for help. This short pastoral answer does not instruct the listener to replace medical treatment with anointing.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer an objection to his interpretation of 2 Peter 3?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes the destruction he reads in 2 Peter 3:5–6 from Noah’s flood and identifies it with the end of a first earth age. He recommends his Three Earth Ages teaching and advises against becoming discouraged by opposition.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer being judged by possessions rather than character?

answers.summary: Arnold cites Acts 10:34 and says God does not rank people by possessions. He encourages valuing the relationship with God over approval from materially motivated friends.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer concerns about military service and evil orders?

answers.summary: Arnold defended honorable military service and referred to Psalm 144, while saying a person need not follow an order known to be evil. This preserves his teaching and does not supply legal advice about military orders.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer concerns that Job’s first children did not receive a happy ending?

answers.summary: Arnold believed they were with God and had moved beyond flesh life into perfection. He said their deaths in the story did not establish that they were wicked or lacked a good outcome.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer how a sinless Christ could come through Adam’s line?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes Christ’s own conduct from Adam’s and directs the listener to 1 Corinthians 15:45–48 for further study.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer questions about Abraham’s second wife and Hagar’s son?

answers.summary: Arnold identifies Keturah, Ishmael and Midian, then relates Moses’ marriage to that family. He describes Hagar and Ishmael as Arab rather than supplying a specific later religion, so that part of the listener’s question remains unresolved.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer questions about the rank and number of angels?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized God’s impartiality and differing gifts and duties rather than naming a highest-ranking creature or giving a count. He said greater gifts carry greater responsibility and believed all souls were created together.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer someone preferring spiritual to religious as a label?

answers.summary: Arnold approves the listener’s distinction and advises judgment in dealing with adversaries. He relates it to his emphasis on Christianity as reality and on the future testimony, not a rule requiring a particular self-description.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer someone wanting to join his church?

answers.summary: Arnold tells the listener to take acceptance up with Christ rather than the ministry. He gives no membership enrollment procedure in this brief answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer someone who felt called to minister but was not doing it?

answers.summary: Arnold suggests readiness becomes evident when people seek the person’s scriptural answers. He cautions against assuming a feeling alone establishes readiness.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer the question about Satan’s short season in Revelation 20:3?

answers.summary: Although the listener names Revelation 20:3, Arnold discusses a five-month period before captivity and cites Revelation 9 and 12. The answer does not clearly resolve the post-millennium period named in the question; the distinction remains flagged rather than merged into a single timetable.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer when communion would be broadcast?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to the next historical broadcast in that time slot. No current communion date is inferred from the recording.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether ancient reports of visitors from the sky all describe fallen angels?

answers.summary: Arnold warned of supernatural deception by Satan but did not identify every reported visitor as fallen. He contrasted evil visitors with his interpretation of God’s appearance in Ezekiel. These identifications are attributed interpretations, not verified accounts.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether believers should keep feast days now?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to Colossians 2 and distinguishes sacrifices and offerings from the love he says God wants. He describes love as the offering in the millennium.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether Cain would have been a giant?

answers.summary: Arnold associates Cain with Sargon and says intermarriage reduced size. These are unsupported historical and ancestry claims, preserved only as his stated interpretation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether Christ would return with his scars?

answers.summary: Arnold directs the listener to Acts 1 and the comparison between departing and returning. The answer is too brief to reconstruct a detailed account of scars.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether cruel behavior is caused by Satan or by people themselves?

answers.summary: Arnold says some people deliberately act cruelly and also relates evil to his first-age account. His ensuing support for civil capital punishment is his doctrinal view, not authority for private retaliation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether he baptized in Jesus’ name or in the name of Father, Son and Holy Spirit?

answers.summary: Arnold says he uses a sacred-name form and explains the name of Jesus through his relationship to the Father. The captions do not reliably preserve the complete form he pronounces, so no exact baptismal formula is reconstructed.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether horses sweat?

answers.summary: Arnold says horses sweat and discusses foam after exertion. He then objects to horse meat under his dietary-law interpretation. Further claims comparing horses and pigs are his comments and are not independently biologically assessed.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether Jesus was poor or wealthy?

answers.summary: Arnold argues Jesus did not lack necessities and discusses a wealthy kinsman, Joseph of Arimathea, and traditions of travel to Britain. Those kinship and travel claims are not established by this FAQ. He distinguishes humility from having no money.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether people remain male or female in eternity?

answers.summary: Arnold refers to being like angels and no longer marrying. He emphasizes something better than flesh life without directly settling every aspect of personal gender identity in the answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether repeated troubles mean a Christian is being punished?

answers.summary: Arnold answers in terms of spiritual opposition and using the authority he associates with Luke 10:19. He encourages resisting negative influences. He does not establish a specific cause for the listener’s individual troubles.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether reporting drug dealers is wrong?

answers.summary: Arnold supports reporting harmful dealing but leaves the individual’s decision with the listener. The answer does not supply a personal risk assessment or a reporting procedure.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether scribes changed the law?

answers.summary: Arnold says they attempted to alter its handling and refers to Matthew 23 and 1 Chronicles 2:55. He links the scribes to his Kenite interpretation; the resulting ancestry and record-keeping claims are not treated as established facts about a modern group.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether the antichrist could physically harm those delivered before him?

answers.summary: Arnold argues the false Christ’s claim to be a peaceful savior depends on deception rather than openly murderous behavior. This reports his expectation, not a guarantee of personal safety.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether the elect are judged at the end of the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold responds by locating the elect’s justification in his account of the former age and referring to Romans 8. He connects that with God’s intervention in their lives rather than directly detailing an end-of-millennium judgment procedure.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer whether to disclose adultery with a friend’s husband?

answers.summary: Arnold said the facts mattered, including coercion and genuine repentance. He questioned causing further hurt through disclosure if both participants had truly repented, while admitting he could not give a definite answer without all the facts. This is his qualified historical advice, not a general rule for every situation.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer which language remained after Babel?

answers.summary: Arnold says followers of God retained a language reflected in the manuscripts while others’ language was confused. He does not clearly name the original language in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer why Israel and Judah were separate houses?

answers.summary: Arnold explains the separation through different captivities of northern and southern tribes. He does not separately narrate the earlier political division in this brief answer, so that historical distinction remains unresolved.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer why people go through suffering in flesh bodies?

answers.summary: Arnold gives his first-age explanation of birth as an opportunity to choose and emphasizes human responsibility. His sweeping claims about the causes of all pain are not established medical findings or evidence that an individual caused their suffering.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer why some people seem to face more troubles than others?

answers.summary: Arnold says a broad comparison cannot identify a definite cause and describes God opening or closing doors. He also speculates about differing roles or needs; that speculation is not used to infer the worth of any person from their circumstances.

questions.question: How did Arnold answer why some women cannot have children?

answers.summary: Arnold acknowledges uncertainty, mentions environmental conditions and differing purposes, and leaves the matter with God. This is pastoral comment rather than an individual diagnosis or established cause of infertility.

questions.question: How did Arnold assess the Bible a listener described as first published in 1582?

answers.summary: Arnold said he liked the edition and used one as a cross-reference. Its title is unclear in the captions, so no specific edition is identified here.

questions.question: How did Arnold assess the Dake reference Bible?

answers.summary: Arnold calls it a useful work but objects to commentary favoring a rapture. He prefers the Companion Bible and claims Dake drew heavily on Bullinger. That claimed relationship between the works is not independently assessed here.

questions.question: How did Arnold assess the Geneva and Bishops’ Bibles?

answers.summary: Arnold said he liked comparing older Bibles and urged greater caution about some newer translations. He did not perform a detailed textual comparison of those two editions in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold compare Christ’s return appearance with the antichrist’s appearance?

answers.summary: Arnold says Jesus returns as he departed and describes the false Christ as imitating him. He gives no precise complexion or physical measurements that this caption passage can establish.

questions.question: How did Arnold compare Exodus 20:24 with Jeremiah 7:22?

answers.summary: Arnold proposed distinguishing the time and circumstances of the instructions and discussed gifts of manna and quail. He concluded with Hosea 6:6 and love rather than burnt offerings. His proposed chronology is retained as his explanation, not independently established.

questions.question: How did Arnold connect Ishmael with later peoples?

answers.summary: Arnold associated Ishmael’s twelve sons with Arab peoples and said many later followed Islam. The chapter number in the listener’s quoted reference is incorrect or damaged in the captions; no precise genealogy of modern populations is established here.

questions.question: How did Arnold connect the Passover celebration with Christ’s resurrection?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasizes celebrating that Christ has risen and connects it with the departed being with him. He does not establish a detailed date calculation in this answer.

questions.question: How did Arnold connect the two witnesses with shortened tribulation?

answers.summary: In response to this question Arnold says the period has been shortened from three and a half years to five months.

questions.question: How did Arnold decide whether a child was accountable and ready for baptism?

answers.summary: Arnold emphasized understanding Christ’s sacrifice and making a knowledgeable commitment rather than a fixed birthday. He described speaking with young baptism candidates to assess their understanding and rejected an automatic age-twelve rule.

questions.question: How did Arnold defend the possibility of twins with different fathers?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguished identical from nonidentical twins when defending his Cain-and-Abel interpretation and suggested consulting a doctor or biologist. That distinction does not independently establish the parentage he attributed to Cain and Abel.

questions.question: How did Arnold describe Christ’s body in the millennium?

answers.summary: Arnold described Christ as transfigured and connected the earlier transfiguration with the resurrection. He called it a spiritual body and compared Moses and Elijah, while expressing uncertainty about aspects of Moses’ transformation; the Matthew chapter recalled in the captions is uncertain.

questions.question: How did Arnold describe Christ’s two advents?

answers.summary: Arnold says one advent has occurred and the remaining return begins the millennium. He distinguishes that from the full Godhead dwelling on earth after the millennium and says Christ does not depart again.

questions.question: How did Arnold describe Paul’s mission and credentials?

answers.summary: Arnold describes a threefold mission using Acts 9:15–16 and appeals to Peter’s endorsement in 2 Peter 3. The recalled verse span in the latter passage needs checking.

questions.question: How did Arnold describe the end of the world?

answers.summary: Arnold distinguishes the end of an age from destruction of the earth as a permanent home. He connects Christ’s return and renewal with Jerusalem and Ezekiel 16.

questions.question: How did Arnold describe the future world to a child comparing heaven with Jerusalem or Bethlehem?

answers.summary: Arnold expected a renewed earth more beautiful than those present places, citing Revelation 21:1. He described a pleasant, inhabitable world with what offends removed, rather than giving invented geographic details.

questions.question: How did Arnold distinguish 1 Corinthians 15’s change from Ezekiel 13’s warning?
